title: Sum with for...of
description: Given an array of numbers, return the sum using a for...of loop instead of a traditional for loop.
whatShouldHappen: Initialize a total variable to 0.
Use for...of to iterate directly over values (no index needed).
Add each value to the total.
Return the total.
patternExplanation: for...of iterates over the values of any iterable (arrays, strings, Sets, Maps) — cleaner than a for loop when you only need values, not indices.

title: Count Key Occurrences
description: Given an object, return the total number of own enumerable keys using a for...in loop.
whatShouldHappen: Initialize a counter to 0.
Use for...in to iterate over the object's keys.
Increment the counter for each own key (use hasOwnProperty).
Return the counter.
patternExplanation: for...in iterates over enumerable string keys of an object — always pair it with hasOwnProperty to avoid counting inherited prototype keys.

title: Collect Characters with for...of
description: Given a string, use a for...of loop to return an array of its individual characters.
whatShouldHappen: Create an empty result array.
Use for...of to iterate over each character of the string.
Push each character into the result array.
Return the result array.
patternExplanation: Strings are iterable in JavaScript — for...of gives you each Unicode character directly, handling multi-byte emoji/symbols correctly unlike a regular index loop.

title: Object to Pairs Array
description: Given an object, return an array of [key, value] pairs sorted by key alphabetically. Use a for...in loop.
whatShouldHappen: Create an empty result array.
Use for...in to iterate over the keys.
For each key, push [key, obj[key]] into the result array.
Sort the result array by the key (index 0 of each pair) before returning.
patternExplanation: for...in collects keys in insertion order — when you need a guaranteed order (alphabetical, numeric), sort the resulting array after collecting.

title: Flatten with for...of
description: Given an array of arrays (one level deep), return a single flat array containing all elements. Use a for...of loop. Do not use Array.prototype.flat().
whatShouldHappen: Create an empty result array.
Use an outer for...of to iterate over each sub-array.
Use an inner for...of to iterate over each element of the sub-array.
Push each element into the result.
Return the result.
patternExplanation: Nesting for...of loops is ideal for traversing collections of iterables — the outer loop visits each sub-array and the inner loop drains it into the result.

title: Filter Object by Minimum Value
description: Given an object with numeric values and a threshold number minVal, use a for...in loop to return a new object with only the properties whose values are >= minVal.
whatShouldHappen: Initialize an empty result object.
Use for (const key in obj) to iterate enumerable keys.
Ensure key belongs to obj using Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.
If obj[key] >= minVal, assign result[key] = obj[key].
Return result.
patternExplanation: Using for...in with hasOwnProperty guards enables safe iteration over object properties while filtering values.

title: Count Vowels with for...of
description: Given a string s, use a for...of loop to count and return the total number of vowel letters ('a', 'e', 'i', 'o', 'u', case-insensitive).
whatShouldHappen: Initialize count = 0.
Use for (const char of s) to iterate character by character.
Check if char in lowercase is one of 'a', 'e', 'i', 'o', 'u'.
If so, increment count.
Return count.
patternExplanation: for...of naturally iterates strings by Unicode code points, eliminating manual charAt or index lookups.

title: Sum Even Values with for...of
description: Given an array of integers, iterate using for...of and return the sum of all even numbers.
whatShouldHappen: Initialize sum = 0.
Loop using for (const num of nums).
If num % 2 === 0, add num to sum.
Return sum.
patternExplanation: for...of provides idiomatic, clean iteration directly over array items without index baggage.

title: Find First Index with array.entries()
description: Given an array items and a target value, use a for...of loop with array.entries() to find and return the 0-based index of the first occurrence where item === target. If target is not present, return -1.
whatShouldHappen: Use for (const [index, item] of items.entries()) to iterate over index-item pairs.
If item strictly equals target, return index immediately.
If loop finishes without finding target, return -1.
patternExplanation: array.entries() yields [index, value] pairs, combining the clean readability of for...of with direct access to element indices.

title: Count Capital Letters with for...of
description: Given a string str, iterate over each character using for...of and return the total count of uppercase ASCII letters ('A' through 'Z').
whatShouldHappen: Initialize count to 0.
Iterate through str with for (const char of str).
Check if char >= 'A' && char <= 'Z'.
If true, increment count.
Return count.
patternExplanation: Strings are iterable in JavaScript; for...of iterates over individual Unicode code points cleanly without indexing.

title: Sum Positive Numbers with continue
description: Given an array of integers nums, use a for...of loop and the continue statement to skip all non-positive numbers (numbers <= 0). Return the sum of all strictly positive numbers.
whatShouldHappen: Initialize total to 0.
Iterate through nums with for (const num of nums).
If num <= 0, continue to the next iteration.
Otherwise, add num to total.
Return total.
patternExplanation: Using continue skips the remainder of the current iteration body, flattening nested if-else blocks into clean guard clauses.

title: Join Words with Custom Delimiter using for...of
description: Given an array of strings words and a delimiter string delimiter, use a for...of loop to concatenate them into a single string separated by delimiter. Avoid adding delimiter before the first word or after the last word. Do not use Array.prototype.join.
whatShouldHappen: If words is empty, return empty string.
Initialize result to empty string.
Iterate through words with for (const word of words).
If result is not empty, append delimiter before word; otherwise just append word.
Return result.
patternExplanation: Checking if the string accumulator is non-empty before prepending a separator avoids trailing delimiters and fencepost errors.

title: Extract Defined Values with Nullish Coalescing
description: Given an array items containing any values and a defaultValue, use a for...of loop and the nullish coalescing operator (??) to return a new array where only null or undefined elements are replaced by defaultValue. Falsy values like 0, false, and "" must NOT be replaced.
whatShouldHappen: Initialize an empty result array.
Iterate through items with for (const item of items).
Apply item ?? defaultValue and push to result.
Return result.
patternExplanation: The nullish coalescing operator (??) specifically differentiates null and undefined from falsy values like 0 or "", essential in data normalization.
